These features collectively fit a high-grade infiltrative glioma phenotype more typical of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma than lower-grade IDH-mutant diffuse glioma. Evidence arguing against IDH-wildtype is the relatively young age of 43 years and temporal-cortical involvement, which can be seen with IDH-mutant astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma. Overall, the aggressive enhancement/necrosis/edema/invasion pattern outweighs the age-location counterpoints, so the best estimate is IDH-wildtype.
